# NetworkSecurityAuthzPolicy

`networksecurity.gcp.hfl.dev/v1beta1`

**Gap it fills.** Terraform's `google_network_security_authz_policy`. An authorization policy: allow, deny or delegate (to IAP or an authorization extension) the requests a forwarding rule, a Secure Web Proxy or an agent gateway receives.

**Source.** generated by `hack/discokind` from the networksecurity.v1 Discovery document.

## Notes

Generated by `hack/discokind` from `hack/discokind/kinds.yaml` (`docs/design.md`
section 2.4); its test is `pkg/discokind/kindtest` with the fixtures under
`pkg/controller/direct/networksecurity/testdata/discokind/NetworkSecurityAuthzPolicy/`.

**An agent gateway as the target.** `target.resources` are the API's
resource names, so a policy targets an agent gateway with
`projects/P/locations/L/agentGateways/G` and leaves
`target.loadBalancingScheme` out (the API refuses it for an agent
gateway). With `action: CUSTOM` and
`customProvider.authzExtension.resources` naming a
`NetworkServicesAuthzExtension`, the gateway's requests go to IAP or
Model Armor (fabric's `iap_config` and `model_armor_config`). Config
Connector's alpha kind takes `target.resources` as forwarding rules only.
The fixtures target an agent gateway. The fake checks no target (see
`docs/fake-cloud.md`); it skips live until `networkservices.googleapis.com`
is on in the live-test project.
